messages.content: I need to start looking at flights from Atlanta to Denver for a gallery installation. I have to be at the venue at 8:00 a.m. Tuesday, April 7, so I need to fly out Monday. The condition-report review is Thursday, but they have only said it could end anywhere from 3:00 to 6:00 p.m.

Understood. I’ll compare Monday, April 6, outbound flights and keep both Thursday-night and Friday return possibilities open. Will you be leaving from the gallery downtown for the airport, and do you have a latest acceptable arrival time in Denver on Monday?
Yes, I’ll leave from the gallery downtown. I’d like enough time Monday evening to get to the hotel, eat, and prepare for the morning. I don’t need to arrive especially early in the day.

A midday nonstop is the cleanest fit. The strongest option is Delta departing ATL at 11:20 a.m. and arriving DEN at 12:42 p.m. local time. A United nonstop leaves at 1:48 p.m. and arrives at 3:12 p.m., which still gives you a workable evening but less margin if the flight or airport transfer runs late.
Use the Delta flight as the working outbound. What can I realistically do Thursday if the review runs until six?

From downtown Denver, a 6:00 p.m. finish makes departures before about 8:30 p.m. risky. The latest nonstop I found leaves DEN at 8:55 p.m. and reaches Atlanta at 1:48 a.m. Friday. You would have roughly two hours and fifty-five minutes from the scheduled review end to departure, but traffic, returning equipment, or a delayed meeting could consume that margin.
That is late, but I would consider it if they confirm the review will finish closer to three. Is there an earlier nonstop that works with a 3:00 p.m. finish?

Yes. There is a 6:35 p.m. nonstop arriving in Atlanta at 11:26 p.m. With a 3:00 p.m. finish, that leaves three hours and thirty-five minutes before departure. If the review slips much beyond 4:00 p.m., I would stop treating that flight as dependable.
And what are the Friday choices? I do not want to spend most of Friday getting home.

The best Friday option leaves Denver at 8:15 a.m. and arrives in Atlanta at 1:09 p.m., nonstop. There is also a 10:40 a.m. departure arriving at 3:35 p.m. The earlier flight preserves more of Friday but would mean leaving the downtown hotel around 5:45 a.m.
Compare the prices using the Monday Delta outbound, first with the Thursday 6:35 return, then the Thursday 8:55 return, and then the Friday 8:15 return. Include one checked bag.

Current round-trip totals with one checked bag are $548 for the Thursday 6:35 p.m. return, $512 for the Thursday 8:55 p.m. return, and $476 for the Friday 8:15 a.m. return. The Thursday options avoid another hotel night. The Friday fare is lowest, but once a Thursday-night hotel stay is added, it may have the highest trip total.

Right. The hotel is expected to be about $210 after tax, so Friday is not really the cheaper plan. I still need the gallery to decide. Do any of these fares let me switch the return without a change fee?

The quoted standard economy fares do not carry an airline change fee, but you would owe any fare difference when changing. The checked-bag charge is included in the totals I gave you. None of the three itineraries has been held, and the fare and seat inventory can change before the gallery responds.

Then keep the Monday Delta outbound as the common piece. Make Thursday at 6:35 the preferred return if they guarantee a 3:00 finish, Thursday at 8:55 the fallback if they say no later than 5:00, and Friday at 8:15 if they cannot promise that. Do not book or hold anything.

The working plan is Monday, April 6, ATL to DEN on the 11:20 a.m. Delta nonstop, arriving at 12:42 p.m. For the return: use Thursday’s 6:35 p.m. nonstop if the gallery guarantees a 3:00 p.m. finish; use the 8:55 p.m. nonstop if it confirms completion by 5:00 p.m.; otherwise return Friday at 8:15 a.m., arriving in Atlanta at 1:09 p.m. Current totals with one checked bag are $548, $512, and $476 respectively, before the additional Thursday hotel night required by the Friday option. Nothing has been booked or held.
